author: reek
body: `secret-sort-name` had no caller anywhere in the tree, so both secrets tests passed while it sorted vault names by ADDRESS. It compiled, and `<` on Text was a pointer compare, so the order was whatever order the entries happened to be allocated in. CDX2089 is what surfaced it; this file is what keeps it surfaced.

author: reek
body: The pair is chosen so the two candidate orders DISAGREE. CCE numbers its characters by frequency rather than alphabetically, so `d` sorts before `b` in encoding order and after it in collation order. A sort written with `text-compare` therefore passes a test built from any pair whose letters happen to agree, and fails this one.

author: reek
body: That is the whole point of the file: it does not merely assert that the function answers, it asserts WHICH of the two orders it answers in. Reverting the body to `text-compare a.se-name b.se-name < 0` moves both lines below.
